6.narration_statement: Action is execution. The agent calls a tool, writes an output, sends a message, or updates a record. Something changes in the world as a result. Then the cycle begins again. Quarrying data, evaluating results, deciding what to check next, generating a finding, before it produces a final output.

7.narration_statement: The first type is the reactive agent. A reactive agent responds to its current input using predefined rules. It has no memory of what happened before. No ability to plan ahead. It simply observes the condition and responds. Think of a simple alert agent as Solara. If output at Site 12 drops below 8% of a baseline, send a notification. That's a reactive agent. Fast, predictable, easy to build, but limited. It can't investigate why the drop happened, or determine whether the alert is actually worth sending.

7.narration_statement: The second type is the goal-based agent. A goal-based agent reasons about actions in terms of whether they move it closer to a defined outcome. It plans and evaluates options. It chooses the path most likely to achieve the goal. Solara's Site Performance Investigation Agent works this way. Its goal is to determine why Site 47 under-performed last Tuesday. It doesn't follow a fixed script. It decides what data to pull based on what it finds, adjusting its approach as results come in.

8.narration_statement: The third type is the utility-based agent. A utility-based agent goes further than goal-based reasoning. It doesn't just ask, will this action achieve the goal? It asks, which available action achieves the goal most efficiently, at the lowest cost, and with the highest confidence. At Solara, a utility-based agent managing report generation across hundreds of sites needs to make trade-off decisions constantly. Do I generate a full diagnostic report or a summary? Do I escalate the anomaly or log it for review? It evaluates options against a utility function and picks the best one.

An error condition is triggered, or the agent determines it cannot proceed and hands off to a human.
